proof_summary: For the block \((2,4,2,4,2)\), an occurrence starting from a prime \(q\) would make \(q,q+2,q+6,q+8,q+12,q+14\) all prime. Their residues force one to be divisible by \(5\); analyzing the exceptional possibility forces \(q=5\) (the alternative \(q=3\) would require \(9\) to be prime), so the block occurs only once and hence not infinitely often.
